dengue.name: Dengue
dengue.transmission: Dengue is primarily transmitted through the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes.
prevention: Wear clothing that covers the arms and legs.
Use screens or other measures to reduce mosquito exposure.

malaria.name: Malaria
malaria.transmission: Malaria is transmitted through the bites of infected Anopheles mosquitoes.
prevention: Follow recommended malaria prevention measures when traveling to affected areas.

influenza.name: Influenza
influenza.transmission: Influenza can spread through respiratory droplets and particles from an infected person.
prevention: Stay home when sick when possible.
warning_signs: symptoms that improve and then become significantly worse

covid.name: COVID-19
covid.transmission: COVID-19 spreads mainly through respiratory droplets and aerosols from infected people.
prevention: Wear a mask in crowded or poorly ventilated spaces.
Follow local public-health guidance and vaccination recommendations.

tuberculosis.name: Tuberculosis
tuberculosis.transmission: Tuberculosis spreads through infectious droplets released when a person with active disease coughs or sneezes.
prevention: Avoid close contact with untreated infectious cases.
Follow public-health screening and treatment guidance.

typhoid.name: Typhoid Fever
typhoid.transmission: Typhoid fever is spread through contaminated food or water and poor hygiene.
prevention: Use proper sanitation and hand hygiene.
Follow vaccination guidance in high-risk areas.

hepatitis.name: Hepatitis
hepatitis.transmission: Hepatitis can spread by contaminated food or water, blood, or body fluids depending on the type.
prevention: Practice safe sex and safe injection practices.
Use clean water and hygiene practices.
Follow medical vaccination guidance when available.

cholera.name: Cholera
cholera.transmission: Cholera is spread through contaminated water and food.
prevention: Use proper sanitation and waste disposal.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.transmission: Pneumonia can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi and may spread through respiratory droplets.
prevention: Follow vaccination and treatment guidance when appropriate.

diabetes.name: Diabetes
diabetes.transmission: Diabetes is not spread from person to person; it is a chronic metabolic condition influenced by genetics and lifestyle factors.
prevention: Follow clinical guidance for weight and lifestyle management.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.transmission: Asthma is not infectious and is not transmitted from person to person.
prevention: Avoid triggers such as smoke, dust, and pollen.
Keep indoor air clean and ventilated.
Seek regular follow-up with a clinician.

piles.name: Piles (Hemorrhoids)
symptoms: pain or discomfort around the anus
bright red blood during bowel movements
piles.transmission: Piles are not infectious and do not spread between people.
prevention: Eat fiber-rich foods and drink enough water.
Do not sit on the toilet for long periods.
Stay physically active and treat constipation with clinical guidance.

tonsillitis.name: Tonsillitis
tonsillitis.transmission: Infectious tonsillitis can spread through respiratory droplets and close contact, depending on its cause.
prevention: Avoid sharing cups, utensils, or toothbrushes.
Stay home while feverish and follow clinical treatment advice.

common_cold.name: Common Cold
common_cold.transmission: The common cold is usually caused by respiratory viruses that spread through droplets, close contact, or contaminated surfaces.
prevention: Improve ventilation and avoid close contact while unwell.
Rest and drink fluids while recovering.
warning_signs: fever that is persistent or worsening
symptoms that improve and then become significantly worse
